stem: During a review, a 16-year-old says yes to using alcohol to relax or fit in, using substances while alone, and forgetting things while using them; what is the best interpretation?

options.text: This pattern can be ignored if the young person is still passing at school
These answers are only significant if there has also been police trouble
These are concerning CRAFFT responses and support a fuller adolescent drug and alcohol assessment rather than reassurance alone
The answers suggest cannabis withdrawal rather than broader substance risk
CRAFFT is mainly a vaping screen, so alcohol-related answers are less useful

explanation: Concerning CRAFFT responses should prompt a fuller adolescent drug and alcohol assessment. Multiple positive responses indicate possible substance-related harm and risk, so the next step is a broader review rather than reassurance alone.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because school performance does not rule out clinically important substance-related risk.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because police trouble is not required for positive screening responses to be meaningful.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because multiple positive CRAFFT responses indicate concerning substance use behaviours and should lead to a more comprehensive adolescent drug and alcohol assessment.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because these are screening responses about substance use behaviour, not a diagnosis of cannabis withdrawal.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because CRAFFT is a general adolescent alcohol and drug screen, not a vaping-only tool.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
